goals.name: 请求退出客户端应用
behavior: CZe defines At with localized Quit appName and role:quit. It supplies At through jt/appMenu on isMacOS; on other platforms it appends an At copy with Ctrl+Q to File only when its submenu was obtained.

No click implementation is present in At: dispatch of the native quit role is a runtime dependency. The already-published eZe lifecycle contract is reused for first-party before-quit/will-quit handling, without asserting that a native menu activation delivered these events.

eZe first applies its native privacy guard, then activity/platform/confirmation conditions. A cancelled confirmation prevents quitting. The ordinary and skip-drain branches differ in settingsStore.flush; neither source promises durable completion of every provider.

The initial Promise.allSettled group has no overall timeout. Only subsequent context cleanup uses the saved five-second u7 contract; synchronous failures, pending promises and the reentry latch retain the published behavior.
conditions: Supplied isMacOS, successful runtime menu construction and File submenu lookup; lifecycle registration, injected activity predicates, confirmation preference and native privacy guard.
failureAndCancellation: The menu schema alone cannot prove OS exit, window closure, backend completion or persistence. Lifecycle rejection/throw/hang distinctions remain as recorded in shutdown-persistence.json.
knownGaps: Native quit-role event delivery and actual process exit; real activity/confirmation state; provider cleanup, timeout and durability effects; standalone runtime qualification.

goals.name: 控制应用及其他应用的可见性
behavior: CZe supplies Hide appName/Hide Others/Show All descriptors with native roles hide/hideOthers/unhide inside jt. Nt consumes jt as an appMenu submenu; Ut includes Nt only when supplied isMacOS is true.

These three intents form one OS application-visibility goal with three operations. No first-party click handler, hidden-window registry or visibility-state persistence is defined by these descriptors.
The labels and role strings identify requested actions; effective process/window scope, OS permissions and resulting visibility remain native runtime contracts to verify.

knownGaps: Owl/native role implementation and distribution; actual Hide/Hide Others/Show All effects and focus; platform restrictions.

goals.name: 在浏览器页面历史中后退或前进
behavior: Ft contains two I generator calls using te(navigateBrowserBack/Forward) and callbacks that invoke Ve with go-back/go-forward. Ft is inserted in the Browser submenu only under u.browserPane.

te applies F to the selected keymap bindings; F rejects space-containing accelerators, values for which i.Lt returns true, and normalized protected keys in P. I creates one hidden item per retained accelerator with acceleratorWorksWhenHidden:true and the same callback. Empty or multiple retained bindings therefore produce zero or multiple items, not fixed cardinality.
Ve returns false immediately if getFocusedWebContents is null. It uses only a valid non-destroyed focused BrowserWindow when one exists, otherwise all windows; destroyed windows are skipped.

G(window) obtains the injected handler browserHostManager. Ve delegates runFocusedVisiblePageCommand(window,focusedWebContents,command), stopping .some only for exact true. Missing manager or non-true result does not establish handling.

Both callbacks discard the Ve return. They neither await it nor invoke ensurePrimaryWindowVisible, renderer app history or thread-list navigation as fallback. History-stack availability and page navigation execution remain at the injected native manager boundary.
conditions: u.browserPane; effective keymap/protected-accelerator filtering; focused webContents, window lifetime and injected browserHostManager.
failureAndCancellation: No focused webContents returns false. Missing manager/non-true result may leave command unhandled; manager throws escape the selected callback. No menu enabled predicate based on canGoBack/canGoForward is supplied by these two option objects.
knownGaps: Effective browserHostManager/native page history implementation; history stack, focused-visible-page selection, failed navigation and actual shortcuts; independent runtime qualification.

mechanisms.name: Services

mechanisms.knownGap: Actual service list, eligibility and invocation are native dependencies; no individual service feature is invented.
mechanisms.scopeQualification: Classifies only this integration/container descriptor, not all child or OS service capabilities.

record.claim: The selected Program-bound eZe caller injects globalState and settingsStore from the same local startup result V, whose initializer is await g.U(...). It injects the vXe facade cleanup and a locally declared stop helper. This proves a source wiring, not an observed Electron quit.
before-quit first calls hd(); a truthy result prevents the event immediately, before checking active work or prompting. The native privacy-query implementation is not executed.

The local-running predicate, non-failed/non-created pending-worktree predicate, and ACTIVE automation predicate are computed. Windows, approved temporary quit, disabled confirmation, or absence of all three activity classes marks app quitting without a dialog.

For the remaining branch, showMessageBoxSync result other than zero prevents quitting. Zero calls markQuitApproved and markAppQuitting. Dialog and localization internals are external to this selected behavior scope.
The captured S flag prevents activation handling after an allowed before-quit or any will-quit. Canceled/privacy-prevented before-quit does not set S in those selected branches.

will-quit sets S true, and returns immediately if captured x is already true. The first handled invocation sets x true after preventDefault and before disposing both lifecycle managers; a later invocation does not repeat the drain.

The ordinary will-quit branch disposes hotkey then dictation, invokes globalState.flush, settingsStore.flush, stopCodexMicro, and flushTracingBeforeQuit in array evaluation order, and waits on Promise.allSettled. The Promises may run concurrently after invocation.

shouldSkipDrainBeforeQuit selects a group that still invokes globalState.flush, stopCodexMicro and flushTracingBeforeQuit, but omits settingsStore.flush. It retains both lifecycle disposals and the later context cleanup.

Promise rejections in the initial allSettled group do not prevent its fulfillment continuation. Synchronous throws during manager disposal or array construction escape this event callback, skipping subsequent calls; x has already been latched.

No timeout wraps the initial allSettled group in this function. Only after that group settles does the continuation invoke u7(flushAndDisposeContext,l7), then dispose the outer disposables and call app.quit on fulfillment. l7 is 5000 milliseconds.

The continuation uses a fulfillment-only .then after u7. u7 synchronous callback errors become rejection and do not take that fulfillment path; a synchronous outer disposables.dispose error also prevents the following app.quit call.

u7 sets a timeout before invoking the callback, then attaches the same fulfillment resolver to both fulfillment and rejection of its returned Promise. Async rejection is converted to fulfillment; timeout fulfills without canceling ongoing callback work. A synchronous callback throw or non-thenable .then access rejects the outer Promise and leaves the timer scheduled.

dependencyPolicy.qualification: Native menu roles, lifecycle event delivery and page-history manager remain dependencies. First-party template/guard/delegation source is retained; no native implementation is copied or assumed equivalent to public Electron.

limits: Native role names prove descriptors and requested intent; actual OS/window/lifecycle/history effects remain unobserved.
Existing shutdown source/fixture evidence is reused, not repeated or promoted to product exit/durability verification.
Browser page history, application router history and adjacent-thread selection have different owners and contracts.
Four integration/container records receive mechanism dispositions without invented user or support operations.
The three new goals have unknown mode ownership; no whole-feature exclusion or standalone runtime/build acceptance is established.
